newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL noon rubber quoted up at noon but trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: KL noon rubber quoted up at noon but trade quiet.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were higher at noon but the market was quiet with traders wary of the uncertainties in a new week and the softening ringgit.
The closure of the Tokyo futures market for a holiday has also left the local market without direction, said traders.
"With Tokyo closed, and being a Monday morning, there're no leads," said a trader.
"But the ringgit is still weak and that's worrying to us, as most of Malaysian rubber is traded in ringgit and not U.S. dollars," he added.

At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted the benchmark RSS1 buyer for August at 237.50 cents (90 U.S. cents) a kg, up 1.50 cents from Friday's close. The SMR20 buyer for August was up one cent to 238.
Traders quoted Wednesday price levels, putting the SMR 20 at 240 cents, SMR CV at 295, SMR L at 276, SMR5 at 248, SMR10 at 242 and drum latex at 193.
At 0500 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6305 against the U.S. dollar.
